subject: Acme Health — Buying process playbook & steering committee ask
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acmehealth.com>, John Sanders <john.sanders@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed stakeholder map and next steps

Hi Emily / John,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — really appreciated the candid discussion on your latency targets and data residency constraints. As promised, I put together a short playbook to help structure the internal approvals and procurement path so you can see what a 6–8 week pilot would look like.

Top-line recap from our call:
- Pilot goal: integrate Redwood Dedicated for anonymized PHI workloads (non-production) to validate latency (<=200ms p99) and cost per 1M tokens.
- Must-haves: SOC 2 evidence, VPC peering, KMS integration, and an audit log retention policy aligned with your compliance team.
- Decision criteria: latency SLO, predictable committed capacity pricing, and demonstrable KV caching improvements.

Attached: redwood-trial-playbook-v1.pdf (high-level timeline + stakeholder map) and a very early SOW template (acme-sow-draft-v1.docx) to kick off procurement language.

As a practical next step, can we lock a 30–45 minute steering committee prep call the week of Nov 16? I suggest the following attendees on your side:
- Economic buyer: John Sanders (confirmed)
- Security lead: Emily Cho (security/compliance)
- Procurement rep: procurement@acmehealth.com (TBD)

On our side I’ll bring Marissa (Customer Success lead) and Neha (Solutions/infra). Proposed times: Nov 16, 11:00–11:45am PT or Nov 17, 9:00–9:45am PT. Please confirm which works and whether I should prepare a one-page decision brief for your execs.

Thanks — happy to iterate on the SOW language if legal/procurement want different wording.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-trial-playbook-v1.pdf, acme-sow-draft-v1.docx
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: John Sanders <john.sanders@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed stakeholder map and next steps

Thanks Marcus — this is very helpful and aligns with what I heard internally.

A couple quick notes from the security/compliance side:
- We need a copy of the SOC 2 report and a short note on where audit logs are stored and how long retention is configurable.
- KMS integration sounds good; our infosec will want to confirm key rotation policies.

From procurement: we typically require a 60-day lead time from an executed SOW for reserved capacity commitments. John, is that accurate?

I can make Nov 17, 9:00–9:45am PT work for a steering committee prep. Please add a one-page decision brief targeted at our VP of Platforms — 2 slides max (cost/benefit + risks & mitigations).

Emily Cho
Director, Security & Privacy | Acme Health
emily.cho@acmehealth.com

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed stakeholder map and next steps

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround and the guidance. I copied procurement directly.

Action items I’m taking and what I need from your side:
1) SOC 2 + audit logs: I’ve attached the specific SOC 2 excerpt and a short note on audit log retention and storage (see redwood-trial-playbook-v1.pdf, page 4). If your team wants a formal SOC 2 package we can run an NDA and share the full report.
2) SOW language: attached acme-sow-draft-v1.docx — I highlighted the reserved capacity clause and a 60-day start-to-committed-capacity timeline. If you have specific procurement terms (PO process, invoicing cadence) please flag them so Marissa can update the SOW.
3) Steering committee prep: Nov 17, 9:00–9:45am PT confirmed. I will prepare the 2-slide decision brief and circulate by EOD Nov 16.

Marissa / Neha — can you join the prep and be ready to run the pilot scope and technical checklist? I also added a short stakeholder map below for the meeting:
- Economic buyer: John Sanders (VP of Product Operations) — cares about predictable pricing, committed throughput
- Security: Emily Cho (Director, Security & Privacy) — needs SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, data residency assurances
- Procurement: procurement@acmehealth.com — standard PO + 60-day lead time
- Platform engineering: TBD (likely infra team) — will own integration and network peering

Thanks all — I’ll share the decision brief and SOW updates tomorrow.

Marcus
